title: fix: prevent SQLite admission refusals during Gateway delays
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat turns and task lists failing with "SQLite transaction admission was refused" when a busy Gateway takes longer than five seconds to service a worker authority request.

## User Impact

Accepted database operations wait for the live owner's decision instead of failing solely because the host was delayed. Revoked authority still refuses the operation. No configuration, schema, durability, retention, or permission changes; updating requires no migration or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker independently expired a request that the host still owned, preventing a later valid grant. Keep the shared decision pending until the host grants or refuses it. Broker failure still terminates and joins the worker before releasing custody; coordinator-lock and broker-capacity deadlines are unchanged. This also removes the race between a late host grant and worker-side refusal.

## Evidence

- Production task-list/chat failures identify this exact refusal path during host scheduling delays; those logs do not measure the precise blocked interval.
- Deterministic regression: the original implementation fails all three delayed-decision cases. The fix preserves successful admission, revoked-owner refusal, and closure without mutation. No real sleeps or test-only production hooks.
- Focused admission, physical-alias/revocation, broker cancellation/capacity, and settlement-cleanup suites: **35/35 tests pass**, four files, 88.49 seconds wrapper wall including cold worker compilation.
- Changed test file: **14/14 pass**, 2.59 seconds Vitest / 4.92 seconds wrapper wall with one worker. These are preserved results from original SQLite head `2374731264e`; the prior recovery verified all three affected SQLite files and their patch byte-identical at `6472c860283`. This continuation did not rerun those tests.
- Fresh standalone AutoReview completed on exact commit `6472c860283613f0d81ba5cfee5d17d6803348b5`: **scoped-clean, no P0-P2 findings**, exit 0. The supplied unchanged-source context and binary patch hashes were verified against the candidate. Earlier authentication failures produced no passing evidence and are superseded by this completed run.
- Personal source inspection and the completed exact-head ClawSweeper review found no actionable SQLite defects. Inspected host current-authority checks, transaction/commit ordering, caller/worker paths, admission service retention, worker retirement, and settlement cleanup. The ECMAScript `Atomics.wait` contract confirms an omitted timeout waits indefinitely and the compare-before-wait handles a decision arriving before suspension.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35590202404) completed successfully on `6472c860283613f0d81ba5cfee5d17d6803348b5`. Required CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review gates are successful; the observed rollup has 168 passing and 43 skipped/neutral checks, with no failing or pending checks.
- Formatting, diff checks, and production typechecking passed in the preserved proof; this continuation also verified the candidate diff has no whitespace errors. Live deployment and chat verification remain the deployment owner's next step and are not claimed here.

### Earlier CI failure and conflict resolution

The original CI shard failed [Discord audio-worker pacing](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35583806686/job/106282792404) because fixture readiness preceded real audio consumption. The original shard replay passed 289 files / 4,079 tests; that passing replay alone did not resolve the race.

Main subsequently landed the owning first-packet readiness correction in [761725d03f2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/761725d03f294aaddc399a759a0755d34a0e1ecf). This PR is based on that correction and drops its redundant Discord test commit. The resulting diff is SQLite-only: one production file, its regression test, and matching documentation. Upstream owns the Discord fixture and its repeatability evidence; no thresholds are weakened by this PR.
